fields.value: No sustained physical description; his presence is defined chiefly through expression, reserve, and speech.
Intelligent, sarcastic, detached, affectionate toward Elizabeth, and too willing to substitute amusement for responsibility.
To protect his privacy and enjoy absurdity, though crisis exposes the cost of disengagement.
Owner of Longbourn, father of five daughters, and husband in an unequal marriage; the estate is entailed to Mr Collins.
Not stated; middle-aged and married for more than twenty years.
Family authority whose wit attracts Elizabeth but whose failures help create the Lydia crisis.
Husband of Mrs Bennet; father of Jane, Elizabeth, Mary, Catherine, and Lydia.
Confronts the consequences of parental negligence during Lydia’s disappearance, though his reform remains limited.
Elizabeth: favourite daughter and intellectual ally. Mrs Bennet: spouse he often mocks. Lydia: daughter whose risk he underestimates.
